stem: Which finding is more characteristic of left-sided heart failure than isolated right-sided heart failure?

options.B: Peripheral edema with distended neck veins
options.C: Dependent leg swelling without respiratory symptoms
options.D: Dyspnea and difficulty breathing when lying flat from pulmonary congestion

rationale: NHLBI lists trouble breathing and inability to sleep lying flat among characteristic symptoms of left-sided heart failure. Right-sided heart failure is more strongly associated with systemic venous congestion, including swelling of the ankles, legs, abdomen, and neck veins.
educational_objective: Differentiate left-sided heart failure, which commonly produces pulmonary congestion and dyspnea, from right-sided heart failure, which more often produces systemic venous congestion.
source_organization: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI), NIH
source_locator: People who have left-sided heart failure; People who have right-sided heart failure
source_claim_supported: Left-sided heart failure commonly causes trouble breathing and orthopnea; right-sided heart failure is associated with swelling of the ankles, feet, legs, abdomen, and neck veins.
correction_summary: Removed the family-member framing and the unsupported requirement for crackles in the source locator. Final item uses directly documented left-versus-right symptom patterns from NHLBI.
audit_findings: D is the left-sided pattern documented by NHLBI. A, B, and C are manifestations of systemic venous congestion and are more characteristic of right-sided failure. No second answer remains.
